detail.body:
## Motivation

Enable dynamic EPLB on Ascend through the existing placement planner and single-layer migration algorithm.

NPU expert weights can use NZ storage, and DeepEP receiver counts can include graph padding. The NPU adapters collect valid sender routes and prepare expert weights for migration while preserving the addresses used by captured graphs.

## Changes

- Use the select-experts gatherer for exact Ascend DeepEP routing counts.
- Reuse the TP device group for statistics and weight transfers. Its ordered members must cover WORLD; migration requires TP = EP = WORLD. Warm collective and peer channels before serving.
- Keep draft forwards and NPU draft graph capture outside the target recorder's reset/append lifecycle.
- Select participating layers/ranks, reuse receive buffers across compatible layers, and bound queued staging work with completion events.
- Keep the existing NZ-to-ND conversion and in-place writeback path on Ascend 910C.
- Add physical-storage staging for Ascend 950PR and 950DT, selected through the existing ARCH35 check.

The shared single-layer migration algorithm is unchanged. No dedicated EPLB communication group is created.

## How to enable dynamic EPLB

Use a checkout containing this PR with an MoE model and NPU backend that provide expert routing statistics and expert-weight updates. Add the following flags to the existing `python -m sglang.launch_server` command:

```bash
--enable-eplb \
--expert-distribution-recorder-mode stat
```

`--enable-eplb` enables automatic rebalancing and weight migration. When the recorder mode is omitted, argument resolution sets it to `stat`; it is written explicitly here to make the configuration clear. Setting the recorder mode alone collects statistics but does not enable automatic rebalancing.

### Parallelism and redundant experts

This implementation requires **TP = EP = WORLD**, with TP members in WORLD rank order and EP greater than one. For a service with 16 NPU ranks, use `--tp-size 16 --ep-size 16`. In a disaggregated deployment, this requirement applies separately to the prefill service and the decode service.

Redundant experts are optional. With zero redundant experts, EPLB can move existing experts between ranks. To give the planner extra replica slots for hot experts, add:

```bash
--ep-num-redundant-experts 16
```

This allocates **16 additional expert slots per MoE layer across the whole EP group**, not 16 per rank. The routed expert count plus the redundant expert count must be divisible by EP size. For example, 256 routed experts with EP16 occupy 16 slots per rank; adding 16 redundant slots increases this to 17. Fused shared experts are separate from these redundant routed-expert slots.

Redundant slots consume additional weight memory and must be configured at startup. For an OFF/ON comparison, keep their count the same in both runs.

### Update interval and statistics window

| Flag | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--eplb-rebalance-num-iterations I` | Number of target-model forward iterations between rebalance cycles | `1000` |
| `--expert-distribution-recorder-buffer-size W` | Capacity of the statistics window used to compute placement | Follows `I` when omitted |
| `--ep-num-redundant-experts R` | Additional routed-expert slots per layer across the EP group | `0` |

Use positive values with **`W <= I`**. These are forward iterations, not requests or seconds. With speculative decoding, a target iteration can produce multiple output tokens. A rebalance cycle does not necessarily move weights: unchanged layers and ranks with no migration work are skipped.

The following PD example uses P `50/50` and D `4000/1000` (interval/window), with 16 redundant slots per role. These are workload-specific starting values from the earlier Ascend 910C experiments, not tuned defaults for 950PR/950DT.

Append to the **prefill** launch command:

```bash
--enable-eplb \
--expert-distribution-recorder-mode stat \
--ep-num-redundant-experts 16 \
--eplb-rebalance-num-iterations 50 \
--expert-distribution-recorder-buffer-size 50
```

Append to the **decode** launch command:

```bash
--enable-eplb \
--expert-distribution-recorder-mode stat \
--ep-num-redundant-experts 16 \
--eplb-rebalance-num-iterations 4000 \
--expert-distribution-recorder-buffer-size 1000
```

Keep the placement algorithm at its default `auto` and let argument resolution choose the dispatch algorithm for the configured MoE backend. DSpark can be used alongside EPLB but is not required to enable it.

### Communication, A5 selection, and logs

EPLB reuses the TP HCCL group and its communication configuration. No separate EPLB buffer-size or communication-mode flag is required. Ascend 950PR and 950DT select the ARCH35 staging path automatically; there is no additional A5 enable flag. The real-device validation status of that path is listed below.

Startup logs include:

```text
[NPU EPLB] communication warmup finished: ...
[EPLBManager] system started, will rebalance per ... iterations.
```

Once enough target forwards have run, check the rebalance start/completion logs. For balance diagnostics, optionally add `--expert-balancedness-report-mode server_log`.

## Ascend 950PR / 950DT weight staging

MXFP4/MXFP8 loaders retain transposed NZ views. Passing these views directly to `npu_format_cast(..., 2)` is rejected by the A5 conversion interface. NZ `copy_` also restricts view destinations.

The A5 adapter snapshots complete expert storage with `copy_memory_` into a same-dtype ND allocation. A byte view exposes one row per routed expert to the existing updater. Communication moves packed FP4, FP8 and NZ padding without numerical conversion. Writeback copies the complete snapshot to the original allocation, retaining model dtype, format, shape, strides and graph addresses.

The full parameter base identifies the total expert count. Only its routed prefix participates in migration; fused shared-expert rows at the end remain unchanged. The adapter accepts dense per-expert storage with an outer expert axis, including inner transposes. Padded NZ tensors must retain the full parameter base through the routed-expert slice. Unsupported offsets/layouts and inconsistent chunk storage are rejected before migration.

Raw copies use `non_blocking=True` and the existing stream/event ordering. Staging includes padding and shared-expert suffixes; no A5 latency or memory saving is claimed.

All new A5 production code is in `hardware_backend/npu/eplb.py`. This combined branch retains its existing TP reuse, NPU draft adapters and graph-backend changes.

## Validation

The new staging implementation was checked on CPU with storage/device doubles and the production Python methods:

- 72 combinations of uint8 packed payloads, FP8/BF16 storage, transpose state, padding, shared-expert suffixes and expert placement. Local swaps, duplicate experts and A-to-B-to-A restoration preserve exact bytes and model addresses/strides.
- Three simulated ranks exercise the production P2P construction and wait sequence with byte messages, including cross-rank moves, a redundant destination and an idle rank.
- Invalid slices, offsets, capacity bounds, detached prefixes and incompatible chunk layouts are rejected before raw copies.
- Additional cases cover ND scales, canaries, inference context, sender-only layers and bounded staging lifetime.
- The Ascend 910C staging class still follows the original conversion/writeback path.
- Ruff, formatting, isort and whitespace checks pass.

These checks do not execute NPU kernels or HCCL. The 950PR/950DT path still needs real-device NZ round-trip, P2P, graph-replay and model-accuracy validation. A single-device probe is prepared outside the PR. Test scripts and reports are kept out of the production diff.

## Existing GSM8K accuracy evidence

The following evaluation was collected on Ascend 910C at [`f6ad2f4f`](https://github.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/commit/f6ad2f4f922d0df111dc66153f543a453267455c), with TP communication reuse and draft isolation enabled. These are historical results for the 910C conversion path. They do not validate the new 950PR/950DT physical-storage path.

Evaluated the same **1,319 GSM8K test questions** with `sgl-eval 0.1.3` and its symbolic math scorer. Both runs use DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8, DSpark gamma 5 / verify 6, 16 redundant experts per role, concurrency 16, temperature 0, top-p 1, seed 0, thinking disabled, and a 4,096-token output limit. The question IDs, prompts, reference answers, and generation settings are identical.

| Metric | EPLB OFF | EPLB ON |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Correct / total | 1285 / 1,319 | 1285 / 1,319 |
| Accuracy | 97.42% | 97.42% |
| Request errors | 0 | 0 |
| Truncated responses | 0 | 0 |
| Evaluation wall time | 174.0 s | 271.0 s |
| Prefill / decode rebalances during evaluation | 0 / 0 | 11 / 3 |

The ON-minus-OFF accuracy difference is **+0.00 percentage points**. Extracted final answers match on **1319/1,319 questions**: 1285 correct in both runs and 34 incorrect in both. This accuracy run uses P `50/50` and D `1000/1000` (update interval / recording window), with concurrency 16.

[Per-question answer comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/fa991ea1e6f4515c034e50228827e8e95f9e3241/eplb-gsm8k-20261029/paired_answers.csv) · [Run settings and results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/fa991ea1e6f4515c034e50228827e8e95f9e3241/eplb-gsm8k-20261029/public_results.json)

+"""Ascend EPLB communication and expert-weight migration.
+
+Callers select these helpers after NPU distributed initialization.
+Import torch_npu only when an NPU operation actually needs it.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import time
+from collections import deque
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Callable, NamedTuple
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from sglang.srt.eplb.expert_location import ExpertLocationMetadata
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+_warmed_device_group = None
+
+
+def get_eplb_device_group() -> dist.ProcessGroup:
+    """Reuse TP's device group and its existing communication configuration."""
+    from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+
+    tp_group = get_parallel().tp_group
+    # Shared statistics and migration use WORLD ranks, including root rank 0.
+    if tp_group.ranks != list(range(dist.get_world_size())):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "NPU EPLB requires a TP group covering WORLD in rank order; "
+            "TP subgroups are not supported."
+        )
+    return tp_group.device_group
+
+
+def _get_migration_group() -> dist.ProcessGroup:
+    from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+
+    parallel = get_parallel()
+    # Migration indexes each rank's expert slots; statistics only sum counts.
+    if parallel.tp_size != parallel.moe_ep_size:
+        raise ValueError("NPU EPLB migration requires TP size to equal EP size.")
+    return get_eplb_device_group()
+
+
+def warmup_eplb_communication() -> None:
+    """Initialize statistics and all-peer migration channels before serving."""
+    global _warmed_device_group
+    group = _get_migration_group()
+    if group is _warmed_device_group:
+        return
+
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    world_size = dist.get_world_size(group)
+    if world_size > 1:
+        rank = dist.get_rank()
+        send = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="npu")
+        recv = torch.empty((world_size, 1), dtype=torch.int32, device="npu")
+        dist.all_reduce(send, group=group)
+        ops = []
+        for peer in range(world_size):
+            if peer != rank:
+                ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, send, peer, group=group))
+                ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv[peer], peer, group=group))
+        for work in dist.batch_isend_irecv(ops):
+            work.wait()
+        # Retain the tiny buffers until communication has actually completed.
+        torch.npu.synchronize()
+    _warmed_device_group = group
+    logger.info(
+        "[NPU EPLB] communication warmup finished: ranks=%d time=%.3fs",
+        world_size,
+        time.perf_counter() - start,
+    )
+
+
+def update_expert_weights_with_staging(
+    weights_by_layer: dict[int, list[torch.Tensor]],
+    old_metadata: ExpertLocationMetadata,
+    new_metadata: ExpertLocationMetadata,
+    layer_ids: list[int],
+    nnodes: int,
+    rank: int,
+    log_metrics: bool,
+    update_layer_fn: Callable[..., None],
+) -> dict[int, list[int]]:
+    """Migrate each participating layer through ND storage, preserving model addresses."""
+    from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.utils import is_npu_arch35
+
+    layer_ids, local_updates = _select_expert_weight_updates(
+        old_metadata, new_metadata, layer_ids, rank
+    )
+    if not layer_ids:
+        return {}
+
+    # Both Ascend 950PR and 950DT use ARCH35. Their NZ copy/cast paths do not
+    # accept the transposed expert views used by MXFP4/MXFP8 inference.
+    staging_type = (
+        _PhysicalExpertWeightStaging if is_npu_arch35() else _ExpertWeightStaging
+    )
+    staging = staging_type(weights_by_layer, layer_ids, rank)
+    group = _get_migration_group()
+    world_size = dist.get_world_size()
+    temp_buffers = []
+    missing_experts_by_layer = {}
+
+    for layer, old_placement, new_placement, local_changed in local_updates:
+        weights = weights_by_layer[layer]
+        if not temp_buffers:
+            temp_buffers = staging.create_temp_buffers(weights)
+        migration_weights = staging.load(weights)
+        missing_experts = []
+        update_layer_fn(
+            routed_experts_weights=migration_weights,
+            temp_buffers=temp_buffers,
+            old_physical_to_logical_map=old_placement,
+            new_physical_to_logical_map=new_placement,
+            num_local_physical_experts=old_metadata.num_local_physical_experts,
+            num_gpu_per_node=world_size // nnodes,
+            rank=rank,
+            world_size=world_size,
+            missing_logical_experts_info=missing_experts,
+            log_metrics=log_metrics,
+            group=group,
+        )
+        # Unchanged local slots may still send, but need no writeback.
+        if local_changed:
+            staging.store(weights, migration_weights)
+        # Release this layer's ND references before preparing the next layer.
+        del migration_weights
+        if missing_experts:
+            missing_experts_by_layer[layer] = missing_experts
+    return missing_experts_by_layer
+
+
+def _select_expert_weight_updates(old_metadata, new_metadata, layer_ids, rank):
+    """Select globally updated layers and this rank's participating layers."""
+    from sglang.srt.elastic_ep.elastic_ep import ElasticEPStateManager
+
+    old_placements = old_metadata.physical_to_logical_map_cpu
+    new_placements = new_metadata.physical_to_logical_map_cpu
+    elastic_ep_enabled = ElasticEPStateManager.instance() is not None
+    if not elastic_ep_enabled:
+        layer_ids = [
+            layer
+            for layer in layer_ids
+            if not torch.equal(old_placements[layer], new_placements[layer])
+        ]
+    num_local_experts = old_metadata.num_local_physical_experts
+    start = rank * num_local_experts
+    local_slots = slice(start, start + num_local_experts)
+    local_updates = []
+    for layer in layer_ids:
+        old_placement = old_placements[layer].tolist()
+        new_placement = new_placements[layer].tolist()
+        local_changed = old_placement[local_slots] != new_placement[local_slots]
+        if not elastic_ep_enabled and not local_changed:
+            if not _rank_may_send_experts(old_placement, new_placement, local_slots):
+                continue
+        local_updates.append((layer, old_placement, new_placement, local_changed))
+    # Validate the whole selected chunk, including layers this rank skips.
+    return layer_ids, local_updates
+
+
+def _rank_may_send_experts(old_placement, new_placement, local_slots):
+    """A possible sender holds an expert needed by a changed destination slot."""
+    local_experts = set(old_placement[local_slots])
+    return any(
+        old != new and new in local_experts
+        for old, new in zip(old_placement, new_placement, strict=True)
+    )
+
+
+def _validate_migration_weights(
+    weights_by_layer: dict[int, list[torch.Tensor]], layer_ids: list[int], rank: int
+) -> list[bool]:
+    """Validate chunk compatibility and return its ND staging requirements."""
+    import torch_npu
+
+    def specification(weights):
+        return [
+            (
+                tuple(t.shape),
+                t.dtype,
+                t.device,
+                torch_npu.get_npu_format(t) not in (0, 2) or not t.is_contiguous(),
+            )
+            for t in weights
+        ]
+
+    sample_layer = layer_ids[0]
+    expected = specification(weights_by_layer[sample_layer])
+    if not expected:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"[NPU EPLB] rank={rank} layer={sample_layer}: no expert weights"
+        )
+    for layer in layer_ids[1:]:
+        if specification(weights_by_layer[layer]) != expected:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"[NPU EPLB] rank={rank} layer={layer}: migration weights must match "
+                f"layer {sample_layer} in tensor count, shape, dtype, device, "
+                "and ND staging requirements"
+            )
+    return [needs_staging for _, _, _, needs_staging in expected]
+
+
+class _ExpertWeightStaging:
+    """Validate a chunk and prepare its weights for ND migration.
+
+    load() prepares the tensors that the updater mutates; store() copies the
+    result into model storage without changing addresses held by captured graphs.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        weights_by_layer: dict[int, list[torch.Tensor]],
+        layer_ids: list[int],
+        rank: int,
+    ):
+        # Convert internal formats and pack strided ND before migrating slices.
+        self._needs_staging = _validate_migration_weights(

+        )
+        self._completion_events = deque(maxlen=2)
+
+    def create_temp_buffers(self, weights: list[torch.Tensor]) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+        return [
+            torch.empty(weight.shape, dtype=weight.dtype, device=weight.device)
+            for weight in weights

+
+    def _begin_layer(self) -> None:
+        # Bound queued work before allocating this layer's ND tensors.
+        # Each event follows the preceding layer's P2P waits and writeback.
+        # With two saved events, the fourth load waits for the first layer.
+        # The allocator can then reuse that layer's released ND storage.
+        if len(self._completion_events) == self._completion_events.maxlen:
+            self._completion_events.popleft().synchronize()

+        previous_layer_done.record()
+        self._completion_events.append(previous_layer_done)

+        return [
+            torch.ops.npu.npu_format_cast(weight, 2).contiguous() if needed else weight

+
+    def store(
+        self, weights: list[torch.Tensor], migration_weights: list[torch.Tensor]
+    ) -> None:
+        for weight, buffer, needed in zip(
+            weights, migration_weights, self._needs_staging
+        ):
+            if not needed:
+                continue
+            restored = torch.ops.npu.npu_format_cast(
+                buffer, torch.ops.npu.get_npu_format(weight)
+            )
+            # Keep the storage addresses referenced by captured graphs.
+            weight.copy_(restored)
+
+
+class _ExpertStorageLayout(NamedTuple):
+    num_experts: int
+    storage_elements: int
+    npu_format: int
+
+    def wire_shape(self, weight: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[int, int]:
+        return (
+            weight.shape[0],
+            self.storage_elements // self.num_experts * weight.element_size(),
+        )
+
+
+def _full_expert_weight(weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # get_moe_weights returns parameter.data[:routed_experts]. Its base retains
+    # the complete expert axis, including fused shared experts at the end.
+    owner = weight if weight._base is None else weight._base
+    if (
+        weight.ndim == 0
+        or owner.ndim != weight.ndim
+        or weight.storage_offset() != 0
+        or owner.storage_offset() != 0
+        or weight.shape[1:] != owner.shape[1:]
+        or weight.stride() != owner.stride()
+        or not 0 < weight.shape[0] <= owner.shape[0]
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("A5 EPLB requires a full expert tensor or its expert prefix.")
+    # Expert rows must occupy independent contiguous blocks. Inner transposes
+    # are allowed, but selecting/stepping elements within an expert is not.
+    span = 1
+    for stride, size in sorted(zip(owner.stride()[1:], owner.shape[1:])):
+        if size > 1:
+            if stride != span:
+                raise ValueError("A5 EPLB requires dense storage within each expert.")
+            span *= size
+    if owner.stride(0) != span:
+        raise ValueError("A5 EPLB requires an outermost, contiguous expert axis.")
+    return owner
+
+
+def _expert_storage_layout(weight: torch.Tensor) -> _ExpertStorageLayout:
+    import torch_npu
+
+    owner = _full_expert_weight(weight)
+    storage_elements = torch_npu.get_storage_size(owner)
+    npu_format = torch_npu.get_npu_format(owner)
+    # ND and batched NZ (including C0_16/C0_32) keep experts independent. Other
+    # internal formats must not be split by simply dividing their storage size.
+    if npu_format not in (0, 2, 29, 50, 51):
+        raise ValueError(f"A5 EPLB does not support storage format {npu_format}.")
+    if npu_format not in (0, 2) and owner.ndim != 3:
+        raise ValueError("A5 EPLB requires 3D batched NZ expert weights.")
+    # copy_memory_ copies destination-sized storage without checking source
+    # capacity and uses signed int element counts. Validate before any transfer.
+    if (
+        not 0 < storage_elements <= 2**31 - 1
+        or storage_elements < owner.numel()
+        or storage_elements % owner.shape[0]
+        or storage_elements * owner.element_size() > owner.untyped_storage().nbytes()
+        or (npu_format in (0, 2) and storage_elements != owner.numel())
+        or (weight._base is None and storage_elements != owner.numel())
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "A5 EPLB requires complete expert storage; padded NZ weights must "
+            "retain their full parameter base through the routed-expert slice."
+        )
+    return _ExpertStorageLayout(owner.shape[0], storage_elements, npu_format)
+
+
+class _PhysicalExpertWeightStaging(_ExpertWeightStaging):
+    """Move A5 expert storage unchanged, including NZ padding and packed bytes.
+
+    Only the ND snapshots are viewed as bytes. Model tensors retain their
+    original dtype, format, strides and addresses throughout migration.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, weights_by_layer, layer_ids, rank):
+        super().__init__(weights_by_layer, layer_ids, rank)
+        self._layouts = [
+            _expert_storage_layout(weight) for weight in weights_by_layer[layer_ids[0]]
+        ]
+        for layer in layer_ids[1:]:
+            if [
+                _expert_storage_layout(weight) for weight in weights_by_layer[layer]
+            ] != self._layouts:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"[NPU EPLB] rank={rank} layer={layer}: expert storage layouts "
+                    "must match across the migration chunk"
+                )
+        self._buffers: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+
+    def create_temp_buffers(self, weights):
+        return [
+            torch.empty(
+                layout.wire_shape(weight), dtype=torch.uint8, device=weight.device
+            )
+            for weight, layout in zip(weights, self._layouts, strict=True)
+        ]
+
+    def load(self, weights):
+        self._begin_layer()
+        self._buffers = []
+        migration_weights = []
+        for weight, layout in zip(weights, self._layouts, strict=True):
+            buffer = torch.empty(
+                layout.storage_elements, dtype=weight.dtype, device=weight.device
+            )
+            torch.ops.npu.copy_memory_(
+                buffer, _full_expert_weight(weight), non_blocking=True
+            )
+            self._buffers.append(buffer)
+            # Reinterpret bytes; a dtype conversion would alter FP4/FP8 values.
+            rows = buffer.view(torch.uint8).view(layout.num_experts, -1)
+            migration_weights.append(rows[: weight.shape[0]])
+        return migration_weights
+
+    def store(self, weights, migration_weights):

+            # The full snapshot retains shared-expert rows outside the routed
+            # prefix. Write it back without copy_'s NZ-view restrictions.
+            torch.ops.npu.copy_memory_(
+                _full_expert_weight(weight), buffer, non_blocking=True
+            )

+    tp_group = get_parallel().tp_group

+    if tp_group.ranks != list(range(dist.get_world_size())):

+def warmup_eplb_communication() -> None:
+    """Initialize statistics and all-peer migration channels before serving."""
+    global _warmed_device_group
+    group = get_eplb_device_group()

+        return

+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    world_size = dist.get_world_size(group)
+    if world_size > 1:

I checked this against the installed PyTorch/torch_npu code and ran a 16-rank comparison on Ascend 910C. Reusing TP is useful here: it avoids activating another communication group for EPLB.

The shared accumulator keeps `_communication_group = None`, preserving the existing default-WORLD selection for GPU. The NPU accumulator overrides the property to return `get_parallel().tp_group.device_group`. This reuses an existing group; it does not create an EPLB-specific HCCL group.

`None` does not mean “reuse whichever group already has these ranks.” The installed call paths are:

```text
reduce / broadcast(group=None)
  -> _group_or_default_group(None)
  -> _get_default_group()
  -> GroupMember.WORLD

all_reduce(group=None)
  -> _get_default_group()
  -> GroupMember.WORLD
  -> group.allreduce(...)
```

WORLD and TP are separate ProcessGroup objects even when both contain ranks 0–15. The NPU adapter checks that TP covers WORLD in rank order, so the existing global-rank indexing and root rank 0 remain valid.

For the comparison, both arms first created and used TP, then ran the same statistics and migration operations with either TP or `None`. Each arm started in fresh processes. The table measures additional device memory at the first statistics collective, relative to the already-active TP baseline:

| Configuration | Reuse TP | Use default WORLD |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill configuration: WORLD buffer setting 2048 MiB | 0.00 MiB | 4097.94 MiB |
| Decode configuration: WORLD buffer setting 1200 MiB | 0.00 MiB | 2401.98 MiB |

The measured increase is approximately **twice the default WORLD group's configured `hccl_buffer_size`**, plus a small runtime overhead:

- Prefill: `4097.94 MiB ≈ 2 × 2048 MiB`, with the setting taken from `DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2048`.
- Decode: `2401.98 MiB ≈ 2 × 1200 MiB`, with the setting taken from `HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1200` (`DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE` was unset).

SGLang selects this value from `DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE`, then `HCCL_BUFFSIZE`, falling back to 200. The observed relationship is therefore to the effective WORLD buffer setting, rather than always to `DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE`.

Values are means across 16 logical devices. The statistics tensor was allocated before measurement; PyTorch allocated/reserved memory did not change across this collective. The increase appeared in total device memory usage, which includes communication resources outside the PyTorch allocator. These are communication microbenchmark measurements, not full-service ON/OFF memory deltas.

Both choices passed the statistics checks and 40 layout checks per rank, including sparse exchanges, redundant experts, NZ/ND staging, in-place writeback, and graph replay reading the updated weights. Thus the reason for keeping this parameter is resource reuse, not a claim that WORLD communication fails.

I also checked the migration path: `P2POp` resolves `None` to WORLD in its constructor. With torch 2.10.0 and torch_npu 2.10.0.post6 on the tested device, `batch_isend_irecv` uses the NPU coalescing path and sends/receives through that selected group. It does not switch back to TP.

I would keep the explicit group for all three statistics collectives. Removing it would make NPU statistics activate WORLD even though the existing TP group can handle them. If an application already activates WORLD elsewhere, its incremental memory cost must be measured from that state; the comparison above specifically verifies the already-active-TP case.

+def warmup_eplb_communication() -> None:
+    """Initialize statistics and all-peer migration channels before serving."""
+    global _warmed_device_group
+    group = get_eplb_device_group()
+    if group is _warmed_device_group:
+        return
+
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    world_size = dist.get_world_size(group)
+    if world_size > 1:
+        rank = dist.get_rank()
+        send = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="npu")
+        recv = torch.empty((world_size, 1), dtype=torch.int32, device="npu")
+        dist.all_reduce(send, group=group)
+        ops = []
+        for peer in range(world_size):
+            if peer != rank:
+                ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, send, peer, group=group))
+                ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv[peer], peer, group=group))

+        torch.npu.synchronize()

+def prepare_expert_weight_update(

+    weights_by_layer: dict[int, list[torch.Tensor]],
+    layer_ids: list[int],

+    new_map: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[list[int], list[torch.Tensor] | None, Callable[..., None] | None]:

+
+    Validate the entire chunk before allocating workspaces or moving weights.
+    The callable loads internal-format weights into ND storage, invokes the
+    shared migration algorithm, and writes changed local slots back in place.
+    Receive buffers live only for this chunk and are reused across compatible layers.
+    ND staging keeps only the current layer's conversion results.

+    from sglang.srt.eplb.expert_location_updater import (

+    )

+    elastic_ep_enabled = ElasticEPStateManager.instance() is not None

+        end = start + kwargs["num_local_physical_experts"]
+        old_placement = kwargs["old_physical_to_logical_map"]
+        new_placement = kwargs["new_physical_to_logical_map"]

+            # Keep possible senders; only skip ranks with provably no work.

+            ):

+        if not temp_buffers:
+            temp_buffers.extend(staging.create_temp_buffers(routed_experts_weights))

+    _SelectExpertsSinglePassGatherer,
+    _StatAccumulator,
+    get_global_expert_distribution_recorder,
+)
+from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.eplb import (
+    get_eplb_device_group,
+    warmup_eplb_communication,
+)
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_exec
+
+
+def isolate_npu_draft_recording(forward):
+    """Disable draft hooks and let the NPU recorder skip reset/append."""
+
+    @wraps(forward)
+    def wrapped(runner, *args, **kwargs):
+        if runner.is_draft_worker:
+            recorder = get_global_expert_distribution_recorder()
+            with recorder.disable_this_region():
+                return forward(runner, *args, **kwargs)
+        return forward(runner, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    return wrapped
+
+
+class NpuEplbAccumulatorMixin:
+    """Share TP communication and initialize migration channels before recording."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        moe = get_exec().moe
+        if moe.enable_eplb and not moe.elastic_ep_backend:
+            # Join/scale paths need their own collective initialization order.
+            warmup_eplb_communication()
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    @property
+    def _communication_group(self) -> ProcessGroup:
+        # Resolve lazily so a replaced TP group is used by subsequent dumps.
+        return get_eplb_device_group()
+
+
+class _NpuDetailAccumulator(NpuEplbAccumulatorMixin, _DetailAccumulator):
+    pass
+
+
+class NpuExpertDistributionAccumulator(NpuEplbAccumulatorMixin, _StatAccumulator):
